title: NVMe Fundamentals & Architecture
desc: Why NVMe replaced AHCI/SATA, the host, NVM subsystem, controller and namespace model, the NVMe specification family, and a first tour of queues and commands.

title: Controller Registers & Initialization
desc: BAR0 register map, CAP/VS/CC/CSTS, the enable and ready handshake, admin queue setup, shutdown and reset, NSSR, CMB and PMR.

title: Queues, Doorbells & Command Flow
desc: Submission and completion queues as rings, doorbells, phase tags, command identifiers, the 64-byte SQE and 16-byte CQE, arbitration and the life of one command.

title: PRPs, SGLs & Data Transfer
desc: How the controller finds host memory: PRP entries and lists, chaining, alignment rules, SGL descriptor types, MDTS and the numbers you should derive by hand.

title: Admin Command Set
desc: Identify (CNS values), Create/Delete I/O queues, Get/Set Features, Get Log Page, Abort, Async Event Request, firmware commands and the admin queue's role.

title: NVM Command Set (I/O Commands)
desc: Read, Write, Flush, Compare, Write Zeroes, Dataset Management, Verify, Copy, Write Uncorrectable and the semantics that matter for data integrity.

title: Namespaces & Identify Structures
desc: NSIDs, private and shared namespaces, namespace management and attachment, NSZE/NCAP/NUSE, LBA formats, identifiers and thin provisioning.

title: End-to-End Data Protection & Metadata
desc: LBA metadata, extended vs separate metadata, Protection Information types 1 to 3, guard/app/reference tags, PRACT and PRCHK, and how validators exploit them.

title: Status Codes, Errors & Recovery
desc: The CQE status field, generic and command-specific codes, error and timeout handling, abort, controller reset hierarchy, and what a robust host or validator does on failure.

title: Interrupts, Coalescing & Polling
desc: How completions reach the host: MSI-X vector mapping to CQs, vector 0, interrupt coalescing, INTMS/INTMC, masking, and polled I/O.

title: Power Management & Thermal
desc: NVMe power states, APST, non-operational states, thermal throttling and thresholds, how they interact with PCIe ASPM/L1 substates and D-states, and how to validate them.

title: Security & Data Sanitization
desc: Security Send/Receive and TCG, Format NVM and Sanitize semantics, crypto erase, write protection, boot partitions, RPMB, and how to validate erase guarantees.

title: Reliability, Logs & Telemetry
desc: SMART/Health, Error, Firmware Slot and Persistent Event logs, telemetry, endurance reporting, self-test, and turning log fields into numbers.

title: Multi-Controller, Multipath & Virtualization
desc: Multi-controller NVM subsystems, dual-port SSDs, namespace sharing, ANA, reservations, SR-IOV virtualization support and NVMe-MI basics.

title: NVMe over Fabrics
desc: Fabrics architecture: capsules, transports (RDMA, TCP, FC), Connect and discovery, queues over fabrics, keep-alive and multipath, and what changes versus PCIe.

title: Advanced NVMe Features
desc: HMB, CMB/PMR, Streams and Directives, Flexible Data Placement, Key Value and other command sets, Copy, Computational Storage and the 2.x command-set architecture.

title: SSD Internals Behind NVMe
desc: What the firmware does between a doorbell and NAND: FTL mapping, garbage collection, write amplification, over-provisioning, wear leveling, ECC, power-loss protection and how each shows up at the NVMe interface.

title: Performance & QoS
desc: IOPS, bandwidth and latency relationships, queue depth and Little's law, steady state and preconditioning, tail latency, fio design, and where PCIe/firmware/NAND each cost time.

title: Host Software Stack & Tools
desc: Linux and Windows NVMe drivers, blk-mq and multipath, nvme-cli, sysfs, tracing, SPDK, io_uring passthrough and the tools a validation engineer scripts against.

title: Validation Methodology & Test Design
desc: How to design a principal-level validation strategy: protocol conformance, negative and stress tests, fault injection, power-loss testing, data integrity, automation and metrics.

title: Debug & Triage Scenarios
desc: Principal-level end-to-end scenarios: controller fatal status, timeouts, hangs, data miscompares, performance regressions, link and reset problems, and how to structure the investigation.
